s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions
salient_findings: Bilateral, symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas on panoramic radiography
Expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of cortical plates on computed tomography
key_facts: Two-year-old boy
Progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
Normal vital signs
No lymphadenopathy
Unremarkable routine hematologic tests
Panoramic radiography showed well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas
Computed tomography showed bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions
Thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
Mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
No cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions, matching the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla, with intact oral mucosa, suggestive of fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of multilocular radiolucent areas, although less common in this age group

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of cortical plates, a possible though less likely diagnosis

raw.rationale: The symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla, intact bluish-gray oral mucosa, and bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of the cortical plates are characteristic of Cherubism, especially in a two-year-old boy.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: More commonly unilateral and aggressive, with cortical breaches and soft-tissue extension, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Typically presents with ground-glass appearance on radiographs and is not usually bilateral or symmetrical in the jaws.

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Associated with abnormal hematologic tests and hyperparathyroidism, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Usually presents as a solitary, expansile lesion with fluid-fluid levels on imaging, which is not consistent with the multilocular appearance in this case.
